newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER QUICKEST IN DOWNHILL TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KOSTNER QUICKEST IN DOWNHILL TRAINING.

text.p: Italy's Isolde Kostner got her first look at the Fatschas course on Thursday and liked what she saw as she posted the fastest time in training for a World Cup downhill on Saturday.

Kostner, a winner last weekend on home snow in Cortina, underlined her superb form ahead of the world championships which begin on Monday in Sestriere, Italy as she stormed down the 2.6-km layout in one minute 27.38 seconds.
Regina Haeusl, fighting for a spot on the German world championship squad, was second quickest in 1:27.80 followed closely by her team mate, Olympic champion Katja Seizinger in 1:27.95.
Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg, looking to pad her lead atop the overall standings with her first career downhill win, crossed a respectable seventh in 1:28.72.

Training was delayed for 20 minutes while Germany's Elisabeth Brandner was airlifted off the course and taken by helicopter to a hospital in Ilanz with a badly broken wrist after crashing near the finish line.
Saturday's race will be the first women's downhill ever staged at this Swiss resort. It will be followed by a slalom on Sunday, the two events making up the season's first combined.
